question: Among completed cases, is the average score typical, or does it conceal a broad distribution?
pattern: Panel a contains 1,798 completed disclosures and has its tallest displayed bin at 55.0%–60.0% (257 disclosures). The median is 55.6%, the middle half spans 45.2%–65.9%, and the 10th–90th percentiles span 35.6%–74.5%. The mean (55.4%; company-cluster 95% interval 53.9%–56.8%) is close to the median, giving no reason to describe pronounced skew. Only 36 disclosures score at most 25%, while 173 reach at least 75%. Panel b partitions all DCs: direct: 34,430 (36.3%); inferred: 17,879 (18.8%); unsupported: 42,646 (44.9%).
meaning: The broad centre means that a mean near one-half is not a universal score for every disclosure. Direct support supplies the larger supported component, but inferred support contributes materially. The pooled support rate is 55.1%, 0.3 percentage points from the macro mean: similar overall summaries here despite their different weighting.
limits: The modal bin depends on the displayed 0.05 bin width and is not a fitted population mode. Panel a weights disclosures equally; panel b weights DCs equally and gives longer claim inventories more influence. Neither panel measures factual accuracy or includes the two missing BACE branches.
caption: **Read the figure:** panel a gives each disclosure one observation (20 equal-width bins); panel b pools DC counts, so it has a different weighting. All completed BACE disclosures and all their DCs are retained, including non-disclosure statements. Bar heights are observed counts/proportions; the macro interval is reported below.
